key_insight: A triadic LLM-teacher-student workflow can improve K-12 writing by using the LLM for scalable idea generation while the teacher filters, guides, and validates feedback.
engineering_relevance: The paper offers a deployable collaboration design and evaluation pipeline for building education-grade LLM systems that reduce teacher workload without sacrificing feedback quality.
method: Built a triadic collaboration system for K-12 writing support.
Used a multidimensional evaluation framework grounded in Systemic Functional Linguistics.
Traced suggestion trajectories to study how LLM and teacher feedback affect student revisions.
evidence_signal: The study analyzes 57,954 essays from 10,195 students across 120 schools over two years, providing large-scale empirical evidence for the system.
watch_item: The reported ceiling effect suggests that more linguistic expansion from the LLM can yield diminishing returns, so adaptation to student proficiency is necessary.
paper_title: Double-Edged Sword or Sharp Tool? Designing and Evaluating Triadic LLM-Teacher Collaboration for K-12 Writing at Scale
